mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.4% in the same month signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.4% in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% month-over-month) and a fall in housing starts (HOUST < -2% month-over-month) signals a divergence between income growth and capital spending, which can destabilize consumption and investment, resulting in elevated return volatility and positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > +0.4% AND HOUST < -2% in same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate below 0.1 percentage points for six consecutive months despite steady or rising payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates underemployment growth, which constrains wage inflation and supports corporate margin stability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises < +0.1pp for 6 consecutive months AND PAYEMS does not fall
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.6%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above trend by more than 1.5% for four consecutive quarters signals a durable acceleration in aggregate demand, which boosts earnings expectations and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.7%) in at least 65% of quarters where the condition is met.
